mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% consistently signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate increases > 0.3pp in 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% from 3-month averages signal broad consumer demand weakness that triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% from 3-month average
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% from 3-month average, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 105.0 indicates supply chain disruptions that reduce corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns during supply shock regimes over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In INDPRO < 105.0 periods, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers Federal Reserve tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent unemployment rate increases and non-farm payrolls declines exceeding 0.2pp and 0.5% from 3-month averages signal labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS declines > 0.5% from 3-month average
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and PAYEMS declines > 0.5% from 3-month average, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts falling below 1,000,000 units (1000.0 in thousands) indicates housing sector contraction that reduces consumer wealth and confidence, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1000.0, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 106.0 consistently indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 106.0 for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of such periods.
